metros.name: Toronto
metros.localNote: The most useful thing to tell a Toronto reader is which routes actually get a large item out of the house, because the popular assumption is wrong. The Salvation Army — the charity most Torontonians still picture sending a truck — states outright on its own site that it cannot offer pick-up services and does not accept furniture at all. Talize, Value Village and Dress for Success also confirm no home pickup. In the GTA the verified ways to move furniture are: Habitat ReStore (free curbside, or paid in-home from $150), Furniture Bank (paid full-service in-home from $150, and the fee funds the charity), Royal Furniture Bank (genuinely free pickup, but Peel Region only — Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon), and Diabetes Canada (free pickup, but clothing and small household items only, in sealed bags under 40 lbs). Second point worth making: Value Village is a for-profit retailer that pays a nonprofit partner for your goods, and the partner differs store to store — at the Queen St E centre it is the Kidney Foundation of Canada. That is not a reason to avoid it, but readers assuming they are donating to a charity should know.

orgs.name: Diabetes Canada — Declutter for Diabetes
refuses: Loose items — anything not in a sealed bag or box will not be collected
Bags or boxes weighing 40 lbs or more
Items left on the ground outside a donation bin
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, but only when they have a scheduled run in your area — enter your postal code on their site to check. Items must be in sealed bags or boxes under 40 lb and left on the doorstep; loose items are not collected.
orgs.locationsNote: No storefront — a home pickup service plus a network of clothing donation bins. Bin finder at declutterfordiabetes.ca/dropbox.

orgs.name: Electronic Recycling Association (ERA)
accepts: A wide range of other electronic equipment
orgs.pickupNote: Pickup is offered for larger quantities but is NOT free — charges depend on location, number of items and services required. They say costs are sometimes waived during promotions. Call before assuming a free collection.
orgs.locationsNote: Toronto depot in Scarborough. Toll free 1-877-9EWASTE. No refusal list and no mention of charitable tax receipts on their Toronto page — do not promise a receipt.

orgs.name: Furniture Bank
refuses: Anything showing signs of bed bugs, pest infestation, mould, bodily fluids or deep stains
Large appliances such as stoves and refrigerators
orgs.pickupNote: Full-service in-home pickup, charged as a volume-based fee starting at $150. The fee funds the charity. A free drop-off option at their warehouse also exists, by scheduled appointment.
orgs.locationsNote: Registered charity #87253 1843 RR0001. The warehouse street address is not published on the donation pages — it is confirmed to you when you book a pickup or drop-off slot on their site.

orgs.name: Habitat for Humanity GTA ReStore
orgs.pickupNote: Curbside pickup is free. In-home pickup is a paid service, priced on their donate page as $150 for 3 items or less, $300 for 4-7 items, and $450 for more than 8. Book through the online donation pick-up request form.
orgs.locationsNote: Nine ReStores listed on their own store locator (Brampton, East York, Etobicoke, Finch West, Markham, Newmarket, North York, Oshawa, Scarborough). Confirm hours and addresses at https://habitatrestore.ca/pages/store-locator — the locator loads dynamically and individual store details could not be read.

orgs.name: New Circles Community Services (GLOW clothing bank)
accepts: Very good quality, clean, gently used clothing that is current in style
Seasonally appropriate clothing and shoes for the whole family
orgs.pickupNote: "Pick-up service is not typically available, except by prior arrangement for large drives." Otherwise drop off at the loading dock. No appointment needed within the drop-off hours.
orgs.locationsNote: One location, in East York. Clothing drop-off is Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 10am-3pm only — publish those hours prominently, since turning up outside them is a wasted trip.

orgs.name: Royal Furniture Bank
accepts: Beds, bed frames and mattresses in good condition
refuses: Items with pest damage or mould
Large appliances — refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers
orgs.pickupNote: Free pickup from your home, booked through their online form. Verified on their own schedule-pickup page: "We'll come to you. Schedule a free pickup from your home." Note their homepage separately describes a $300 delivery fee — that fee is charged to the FAMILIES RECEIVING furniture, not to donors. Do not present the $300 as a donor cost.
orgs.locationsNote: One Mississauga warehouse serving Peel Region (Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon). Listed as "Registered Non-Profit No. 1382968-5" — a non-profit number, not a CRA charitable registration, so do not promise a tax receipt.

orgs.name: reBOOT Canada
accepts: Peripherals — hard drives, RAM, keyboards, mice, speakers
orgs.pickupNote: Pickup is for organizations donating 20 or more items only, and fees may apply. Individuals drop off. Back up your data first — devices are sanitized.
orgs.locationsNote: Registered charity refurbishing equipment for non-profits. Drop-off windows are narrow and must be published: Toronto office Wednesdays 10:30am-2:30pm (donations of 20 items or fewer); Brampton depot weekdays 9:30am-4pm (for larger volumes). Street addresses are not on the donate page — link to their site rather than printing an address.
orgs.restricted: Pickup is for organizational donations of roughly 20 items or more, not household drop-offs.

orgs.name: Daily Bread Food Bank
orgs.pickupNote: No home collection. Drop off at the warehouse, at any firehall in the city, or in the yellow bins at participating grocery stores. You can also have an online grocery order delivered to the warehouse during warehouse hours.
orgs.singleAddress: 191 New Toronto Street, Gate 2, Toronto, ON
orgs.locationsNote: One warehouse, Monday to Friday 10:00am-3:30pm, plus firehalls across the city and yellow bins at participating supermarkets. Non-perishable food only — this is NOT a used-goods donation point.

orgs.name: Dress for Success Toronto
refuses: Clothing in need of repair or stained
orgs.pickupNote: "Unfortunately, as a small organization, we do not have the resources to offer pick-up services." Donations are taken 1:00-2:00pm Thursdays, by appointment only.
orgs.singleAddress: 5150 Yonge Street, Unit C29, Toronto, ON M2N 6L8
orgs.locationsNote: One boutique in North York, appointment only. Narrow scope: workplace-appropriate women's clothing in excellent condition. They issue tax receipts only for monetary donations, not clothing.

orgs.name: Talize
orgs.pickupNote: They state: "Talize unfortunately doesn't offer home pick-ups." Every store has a donation centre.
orgs.locationsNote: 15 stores listed on their donate page; the GTA-area ones named are Brampton, Mississauga and Whitby. Donations support charity partners including Cornerstone to Recovery and SickKids.

orgs.name: The Children's Book Bank
accepts: Books for children ages 0 to 18, gently used or new
refuses: Books with water damage, yellowing or tears
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup. Donations are accepted ONLY on specific scheduled drop-off dates at two warehouses, and they explicitly ask that you not bring book donations to their storefront at 585 Dundas St E. Always link to the live donate page for current dates rather than printing dates that will go stale.
orgs.locationsNote: Two donation warehouses: Sherbourne at 334 Bleecker St (416-925-1230) and Morningside at 1154 Morningside Ave (416-214-0837). Main phone listed is the Regent Park HQ. Drop-off dates are occasional, 11:00am-2:30pm — dated and must be checked live.

orgs.name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store, National Recycling Operations
orgs.pickupNote: They state plainly: "We are unable to offer donation pick-up services." Drop off at a store instead. This is the single most common misconception about them and is worth stating loudly on the page.
orgs.locationsNote: They state over 120 locations across Canada. Use their own finder at https://thriftstore.ca/locations rather than listing GTA branches. Tax receipts are issued only for valuables with a fair market value over $500.

orgs.name: Value Village (Savers Value Village)
orgs.pickupNote: No home pickup is offered. Drop off at a Community Donation Centre. Donors get 20% off their next purchase under their Declutter Responsibly program.
orgs.locationsNote: IMPORTANT FRAMING: this is a for-profit retailer that PAYS a nonprofit partner for donated goods — it is not itself a charity, and the partner differs by store. One confirmed example is the Queen St E Community Donation Centre at 924 Queen St E, Toronto ON M4M 1J5, phone (647) 255-7794, whose partner is the Kidney Foundation of Canada. Do not generalise that partner to other stores. Send readers to valuevillage.ca to find their nearest centre.
orgs.notCharity: A for-profit retailer, not a charity. It pays a nonprofit partner for donated goods — the partner differs by store, so ask at the door if that matters to you.

metros.name: Montréal
metros.localNote: Two things worth knowing before you load the car. First, almost every large Montréal collector refuses furniture. Renaissance, Le Support and Entraide diabétique du Québec all say no to sofas, beds and mattresses. For large items the realistic options are Welcome Collective (paid collection, from $50, and the only one that will take a fridge or a stove), L'Entraide Les Ami(e)s de Montréal, Le Chaînon's furniture form, or a city écocentre. Second, the city's écocentres are the fallback for the awkward things the charities turn away: they accept goods in good condition for reuse — antiques, garden items, sports equipment, musical instruments (but not large ones like pianos or organs), toys and games, books, DVDs, records and CDs, furniture and decorative items, hand tools, small electrical appliances, clothing and household linen — and route them to the operator that runs Montréal's reuse centres. Find your nearest one at montreal.ca/sujets/ecocentres. Service is French-first at most of these organizations; Renaissance, Welcome Collective, Insertech and Le Support publish full English versions of their sites.

orgs.name: Entraide diabétique du Québec
accepts: Clothing, clean and free of tears
Small decorative items, lamps, mirrors and frames
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, in their own words: "Nous collectons vos vêtements et articles usagés tout à fait gratuitement" and "Nul besoin de vous déplacer! Nous venons à vous gratuitement." You register through the form on their site, they call you back to agree a date, and on the day you leave the bags at the agreed spot marked with a paper bearing the letter "D" for "Diabète." No time is given in advance — the driver sets it that day. The Mirabel office covers part of Montréal, Laval, the Rive-Nord, part of the Montérégie and the Laurentides: 450 530-7800 or 1 866 313-7800.
orgs.locationsNote: Three regional offices covering southern Quebec (Québec City, Trois-Rivières, Mirabel). The Mirabel office is the one that serves the Montréal area.
orgs.taxReceiptNote: Stated verbatim on their collection page: "Veuillez noter qu'aucun reçu d'impôt ne peut être remis pour les articles donnés. Seuls les dons en argent sont admissibles à un reçu."

orgs.name: Insertech
refuses: Nothing is listed as refused outright — equipment they cannot refurbish is recycled locally instead
orgs.pickupNote: Free pickup is for businesses only: partner companies, or donations of at least 15 computers with an Intel i5 8th-generation processor or better. Everyone else drops off at the back door, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed Wednesdays, no appointment needed.
orgs.locationsNote: One site, in the Angus district of Rosemont.
orgs.taxReceiptNote: Official donation receipts go to eligible companies whose equipment meets their processor and condition standards. Individuals should not expect one.

orgs.name: L'Entraide Les Ami(e)s de Montréal
orgs.pickupNote: They collect furniture and accessories in good condition from homes across Greater Montréal, Laval and the South Shore: "Nous ramassons seulement des meubles et accessoires en bon état." No fee is stated on their site and they do not publish a list of what they turn away, so confirm both when you call. (514) 846-9222 or (514) 507-3200, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed weekends.
orgs.locationsNote: One published address: 3723 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, Montréal, QC H4C 1P8.

orgs.name: Le Chaînon
accepts: Furniture, by prior arrangement through their online form
refuses: Anything not in very good condition — their stated rule is that goods given to the store must be in very good condition and have resale value
orgs.pickupNote: Furniture is handled separately: you fill in the furniture donation form on their site and, in their words, "a responsible person will communicate with you" to arrange the details. No terms or fee are published, so ask when they call. General donations go to the stores during opening hours; phone 514-843-4354 to arrange a large drop-off.

orgs.name: Le Support (Société québécoise de la déficience intellectuelle)
accepts: Clothing and textiles in good condition
Small electrical appliances, including microwave ovens
Alarm clocks, sound systems, cameras, lamps, fans
Board games, puzzles, dolls and stuffed toys
orgs.pickupNote: They do run a home pickup service — their site describes arranging a time and coming to your home to collect what you have to give, booked through an online application. No fee is stated on the pages that loaded, and the booking page itself did not load when checked, so confirm terms and any cost when you book. Call 514 725-9797, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 3:15 p.m., to check whether a specific item is accepted.
orgs.locationsNote: Their site states more than 200 donation bins in the Montréal area, findable with the bin locator on lesupport.ca. They also run two "Les Trouvailles du Support" thrift stores, in Verdun and in Longueuil.

orgs.pickupNote: One of the few Montréal charities that will come for a sofa or a fridge. Their own wording: "Our collection rates begin at $50, and include a sliding scale option." They cover the island of Montréal, the South Shore and Laval; pickups run Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Drop-off is also possible at their Ahuntsic warehouse near métro Sauvé, Monday to Friday 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.

orgs.taxReceiptNote: Their own wording: "Once you complete your donation, you will receive a charitable tax receipt for the value of the donated items by email. Only furniture and appliances are eligible for a tax receipt."

orgs.name: Fondation La Collecte
accepts: Clean, reusable children's and adult clothing
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is advertised. Their site only says "We know it's not always possible to travel to a drop-off location. Contact us to see how we can help" — so whether they will come to you, and on what terms, is decided case by case. Phone (514) 845-7920 ext. 222 or email info@lacollecte.ca to ask.
orgs.locationsNote: Their site states more than 100 donation bins across the Greater Montréal area, with an interactive map on fondationlacollecte.ca to find the nearest. Proceeds go to Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Montreal.

orgs.name: Renaissance
accepts: Clothing, shoes, caps, hats, scarves and shawls
Handbags, glasses, new cosmetics, jewellery, belts
Games, toys, bath rings and seats in good condition
Kitchen articles, lamps, frames, curtains, fabric, bedding
Televisions, DVD players, VCRs, cameras, air conditioners
Sporting gear, books, CDs, DVDs, vinyl records, bicycles
refuses: Large upholstered or non-upholstered furniture (armchairs, couches, chairs, shelves, beds, desks)
Breast pumps, CPAP machines, syringes, medication
Mirrors, fabric scraps, food, company-logoed merchandise
orgs.pickupNote: Call before counting on it. Two Renaissance pages state plainly that there is no home collection: the donation page says "Please note that we do not offer home pick-ups" and the FAQ says "Renaissance ne peut pas offrir de service de collecte de dons à domicile." A third page (their donation-centres directory) points to a home-collection sign-up at collecteadomicile.renaissancequebec.ca, but that subdomain returned no readable content when checked, so the service could not be confirmed. Treat drop-off as the reliable option.
orgs.locationsNote: A large network of donation centres and thrift stores across Quebec, listed by region on their own site with a map at https://renaissancequebec.ca/en/map. No total count is published on the pages read — use their map rather than a fixed list.
orgs.taxReceiptNote: Confirmed on their FAQ: "Renaissance n'émet pas de reçus fiscaux pour les dons de vêtements et d'articles reçus par la population." Exceptions may be considered for very large donations (several hundred or thousand items), where Renaissance sets the value and requires a detailed inventory.

orgs.name: RÉCO (Architecture Sans Frontières Québec)
accepts: Doors at least 29 in. wide and 79 in. tall
refuses: Currently also refused: sinks, bathtubs and painted mouldings
orgs.pickupNote: No collection at present. Their own wording: "Apportez-nous vos articles à notre boutique. Nous n'offrons pas la collecte de don pour le moment." You submit photos and details through their online form first and they validate the donation before you bring it in.
orgs.locationsNote: One location, a short walk from métro Sauvé. RÉCO directs its profits to Architecture Sans Frontières Québec.
orgs.taxReceiptNote: Their own wording: "Lorsque la valeur marchande de vos articles dépasse 500 $, bénéficiez d'un reçu de charité." Items are evaluated within about a month and receipts are issued by year end.

orgs.name: Village des Valeurs
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is mentioned anywhere on their Montréal pages — plan to bring donations to a donation centre yourself. Not every location takes donations, so check the store page first.
orgs.locationsNote: Two Montréal locations are confirmed on their own site as taking donations: 4912 rue Jean-Talon Ouest, H4P 1W9 (514 739-1962) and 2033 boul. Pie-IX, H1V 2C9 (514 528-8604). The Station du Parc boutique does not accept donations. Use their location pages to check others.

metros.name: Vancouver
metros.localNote: Furniture is the real Vancouver problem, and it is worth saying so at the top of the page. Salvation Army, MCC Surrey and the Surrey Community Thrift Store all refuse furniture outright; BC SPCA takes "small furniture items" only and refuses mattresses. A sofa realistically means Habitat ReStore's free pickup, or paying a furniture bank to come and get it - HomeStart (minimum $100; Vancouver, Burnaby west of Royal Oak, and Richmond) or Shelter to Home (minimum $130; North and West Vancouver only, but they do take mattresses, which almost nobody else does). The only genuinely free at-home collections verified are Big Brothers of Greater Vancouver and Diabetes Canada, and both are limited to clothing, books and small household goods - neither will take a couch. Goodwill does not operate in BC; do not list it.

orgs.name: Big Brothers of Greater Vancouver
refuses: No refusal list is published on their donation page
orgs.pickupNote: Their page states: "Free service available for clothing, books, and small household goods. Book a pickup online or call 604.526.2447." Note the pickup is limited to clothing, books and small household goods - not furniture. Bagging/labelling instructions and a pickup time were not confirmed on the page read.
orgs.locationsNote: Donation bins and drop-off points across the Lower Mainland - use the donation bin map on their site rather than assuming a count. They are also the paid nonprofit partner at the Savers/Value Village Community Donation Centre at 6415 Victoria Dr, Vancouver.

orgs.name: Diabetes Canada - Declutter clothing donation programme
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, but only when they have a scheduled run in your area — enter your postal code on their site to check. Items must be in sealed bags or boxes under 40 lb and left on the doorstep; loose items are not collected.
orgs.locationsNote: Donation bins plus the home pickup service - use the "Find a donation bin" locator on diabetes.ca. No Metro Vancouver bin count is published.

orgs.name: Electronic Recycling Association (ERA)
accepts: Media - hard drives, tapes, floppy discs, CDs
orgs.pickupNote: Pickup is offered but is NOT automatically free. Their page: pickup charges are "based on location, the number of items, service requirements, etc.", and may be waived during promotions or for members and high-value donations. Dropping standard computer equipment at the Richmond depot is typically free, but processing fees apply to TVs, microwaves and floor-model copiers and printers. Data destruction is quoted at $0.00-$5.00 per item depending on the equipment donated. Get a quote before loading a vehicle.
orgs.locationsNote: Richmond depot serves Metro Vancouver. Toll-free 1-877-939-2783 (1-877-9EWASTE).
orgs.singleAddress: Unit 1045 - 11111 Twigg Place, Richmond, BC V6V 3C9

orgs.name: HomeStart Foundation
accepts: Chairs and sofas under 80 inches long
TVs under 5 years old, and radios
refuses: Beds - frames, mattresses, box springs, headboards
Large appliances - stoves, washers, dryers, fridges
orgs.pickupNote: Pickup for a minimum $100 donation. Drivers accept cash, cheque or credit card, or you can donate online in advance. Service area as written on their page: "Vancouver, Burnaby (west of Royal Oak) and Richmond". Book by emailing coordinator@homestart.ca to arrange pickup days and times. Note: pickup days/hours and a same-day policy were NOT found on the page read - do not publish specific hours.
orgs.locationsNote: No public warehouse address; arrange by email at coordinator@homestart.ca. Charitable registration 872814504RR0001. No phone number appears on their donations page - do not publish one.

orgs.name: Shelter to Home
accepts: Couches, sofas and love seats, 78 inch maximum
Mattresses, box springs and metal bed frames - twin, double and queen
Bed linen and sheet sets, blankets and comforters - twin, double, queen
Dishes and cutlery, sets of 4 or 6 preferred
refuses: TVs - "We are no longer accepting TVs"
orgs.pickupNote: Their page states: "Once approved, we can pick up from your location for a minimum $130 donation (to cover moving costs)" and "we are able to pick up furniture only from North and West Vancouver locations." Email Info@sheltertohome.ca or phone 778-653-9669 with photos and dimensions to get approval first.
orgs.locationsNote: Drop-off is at a North Vancouver storage facility whose address is given once a donation is approved, not published.

orgs.name: Union Gospel Mission (UGM)
accepts: Weather-appropriate clothing - shirts, sweatshirts, fleece, shorts, pants, jeans, jackets, coats (larger sizes preferred)
Socks and underwear, new and unused only
Shoes - sandals, sneakers, boots, work boots
Bags, belts, cold and hot weather accessories
Pillows and cushions, new and unused only
Small appliances, lamps, knick-knacks, decorations, pictures, wall decor
Small furniture - night tables, coffee tables, small dressers, small bookcases, small dining tables with up to 4 chairs, accent chairs
Children's toys, new and unused only
New, unopened hygiene items, sleeping bags, emergency blankets, rain ponchos, reusable water bottles
orgs.pickupNote: Their page states: "Due to capacity, we are not able to fulfill every request for donation pick-ups." Requests go through the donation coordination form on that page. A pickup is not guaranteed and no terms, area or fee are published.
orgs.locationsNote: Four drop-off points, all listed on ugm.ca/donation-items: UGM Distribution Centre, 8346 St. George St, Vancouver V5X 3S7, Mon-Fri 9am-4pm; UGM Vancouver reception, 601 E. Hastings St, 604-253-3323, 8am-7pm daily; UGM Thrift Store, 671 E. Hastings St, 604-254-8721, Mon-Fri 9:30am-4pm; Found Thrift Boutique, 641 Columbia St, New Westminster, 604-553-0604, Mon-Sat 10:30am-5:30pm. Tax receipts via Donor Relations, 778-731-1611.

orgs.name: BC SPCA Thrift Stores
refuses: Anything restricted by health or safety regulations
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is mentioned anywhere on their thrift store page. Their own instruction: "Because donation needs, storage space and staffing can vary by location, please call ahead before bringing items to a Thrift Store location." They also ask that items not be left outside locations after hours.
orgs.locationsNote: Eleven BC SPCA thrift stores province-wide. The Metro Vancouver ones are Vancouver (East), Vancouver (West), North Vancouver, New Westminster, Richmond and Surrey. Each store has its own phone number - get it from the list at spca.bc.ca/thrift-stores and call that store, not a central line.

orgs.name: Community Thrift Store (Surrey Hospice Society & Surrey Fire Fighters Charitable Society)
accepts: Small kitchen appliances such as toasters, crock pots, kettles
Ornaments, knickknacks, silk flowers, collectibles, artwork
Linen, towels, decorative pillows, pictures, mirrors
refuses: Mattresses, bed frames and large furniture
Baby furniture, cribs and car seats
Blinds, curtain rods, large area rugs
Computers, printers, TVs and microwaves - see note, their page contradicts itself on these
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is mentioned. Drop-off at the store or at donation bins located at Surrey fire halls.

orgs.singleAddress: 7138 King George Blvd, Surrey, BC V3W 5A3

Hazardous materials - all chemicals, grout, mortar, caulk

Third-party directories claiming MCC Surrey collects furniture and large appliances across Surrey, White Rock, North Delta, Cloverdale and Langley are NOT supported by their own site - phone 604-583-0465 before relying on that.
orgs.locationsNote: One Surrey shop, part of the wider MCC Thrift network. Drop-off hours on their site are Tuesday to Friday, 9:30am to 4pm.

orgs.name: Savers / Value Village Community Donation Centre - South Vancouver
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is stated. IMPORTANT for the page author: Savers/Value Village is a FOR-PROFIT retailer. It pays a nonprofit partner for the goods you drop off - at this location the partner is Big Brothers of Greater Vancouver. Donors do not get a charitable tax receipt here. Say so plainly, or readers will assume it is a charity shop.

orgs.notCharity: A for-profit retailer, not a charity. It pays a nonprofit partner for donated goods — the partner differs by store, so ask at the door if that matters to you.

orgs.name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store (National Recycling Operations)
refuses: Infant equipment - car seats, cribs, strollers
orgs.pickupNote: Their own page states plainly: "We are unable to offer donation pick-up services." Drop-off only.
orgs.locationsNote: Their page says "over 120 locations across Canada" - it does NOT give a Metro Vancouver count. Use the store finder at thriftstore.ca to find the nearest one.

metros.name: Calgary
metros.localNote: Calgary's distinctive option is the Calgary Drop-In Centre's Free Goods Program on 11a Street NE — donated furniture and household goods are not resold but given free to Calgarians setting up a home, and their accepted-items list explicitly includes beds. WINS is the other place that takes mattresses; its own page says it accepts "new and clean gently-used clothing, household goods, and furniture including mattresses", though only at its Dover, Glenbrook, Macleod, Manchester and Donation Centre sites. For a sofa, Habitat ReStore is the confirmed free-pickup option in Calgary; WINS will refer you to a paid collection firm instead. Goodwill and Salvation Army both refuse furniture outright, and Salvation Army offers no pickup of any kind. Note for the page author: do not describe Diabetes Canada's clothing pickup as "free" — their site never says so.

orgs.name: Diabetes Canada Declutter Program
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, but only when they have a scheduled run in your area — enter your postal code on their site to check. Items must be in sealed bags or boxes under 40 lb and left on the doorstep; loose items are not collected.

orgs.name: Electronic Recycling Association (ERA)
accepts: Other electronic devices — see their Electronics We Accept page for the full list
orgs.pickupNote: Drop-offs are "often free of charge", though their site notes fees apply to TVs, microwaves and floor-model copiers and printers. Pickup is charged: "Pickup charges are based on location, the number of items, and service requirements," sometimes waived "during our yearly promotions or for members and high-valued donations." Call first for a quote. Working gear is refurbished — "we will donate them to charities across Canada."
orgs.locationsNote: Main Calgary facility below; toll free 1-877-9EWASTE. Hours are not published on their Calgary page — call before going.

orgs.name: Goodwill Industries of Alberta
accepts: New and gently used clothing, laundered and clean
refuses: Furniture over 50 lbs — furniture must go to the Impact Centres or a partner non-profit, not regular stores or donation centres
Upholstered furniture, hide-a-beds, waterbeds, bed frames with springs
Halogen lamps, lava lamps, fluorescent and ceiling lights
Ski and snowboard equipment with bindings
Guns, replica and play guns, ammunition, fireworks
Baby gates, cribs and cradles, strollers, playpens, swings, walkers, bath seats
Medical supplies and personal care items

Hauling to offer donation pickup." They also note the hauler "will also pick up donation items that Goodwill cannot accept." Their site does NOT state whether this is free or paid, and does not confirm Calgary coverage — check availability and cost on their Donation Pickup page at goodwill.ab.ca/donation-pickup/ before assuming anything.
orgs.locationsNote: Their own donation-centre finder at goodwill.ab.ca/donate/ lists 16 Calgary locations, each with its own phone number and hours — use the finder rather than a fixed list, as hours vary by site. Furniture under 50 lbs is only taken at the Calgary Impact Centre.

refuses: Anything exposed to cigarette smoke or pet hair
Mattresses, sofa beds, futons, box springs
orgs.pickupNote: Free pickup confirmed on their donation guidelines page: "You can drop off donations at any Habitat ReStore in Southern Alberta or request a free pickup for larger items." Book via the donation form on their site or call (403) 291-6764 ext. 1. Donation questions also go to calgaryrestore@habitatsouthernab.ca.

orgs.name: WINS (Women In Need Society)
accepts: New and clean gently-used clothing for women, men, children and youth
orgs.pickupNote: No in-house pickup. Their Collector Services page states: "WINS has partnered with select firms that offer professional collection services for a fee." Three firms are named there — The Junk Movement, BE&P Services and Moovez — which you book and pay directly.
orgs.locationsNote: Several WINS thrift stores across Calgary — see their locations page. Their donation information page states: "Please note that large items such as furniture and housewares are only accepted at Dover, Glenbrook, Macleod, Manchester and the Donation Centre."

orgs.name: Bicycles for Humanity - Calgary Chapter

Two drop-off points are listed: Spyhill Landfill, 2142 47 Ave SW — "Drop off in the alley, Accessed is off 20th St. SW", "Any day of the week between 9AM and 5PM"; and BikeBike, 430b 40 Avenue NE, "during business hours". They publish no bike-condition policy, so email calgary@bicycles-for-humanity.org first if you are unsure whether yours is usable.
orgs.locationsNote: Two drop-off points confirmed on their site. All-volunteer, no storefront.

orgs.name: Calgary Drop-In Centre Free Goods Program

Electronics, working or non-working: computers, tablets, monitors, keyboards, mice, cords

Call 403-264-0856 or email donationcentre@thedi.ca before arriving with a large load. Note they state "we are unable to provide a delivery service" — that refers to delivering goods to recipients, which is a separate matter from donor pickup.
orgs.locationsNote: One donation centre. Hours confirmed on their site: "Monday-Sunday: 9 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Closed for statutory holidays."

orgs.name: Little Red Reading House
accepts: Clean, lightly used children's books with minimal wear
Books with pages intact and free from writing or colouring
Books with secure covers and bindings

Books with writing, highlighting or colouring

Books with broken bindings or loose pages

orgs.locationsNote: One Book Bank location. Regular hours are Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. — note this is three days, not Tuesday through Friday. They also run monthly donation days from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.; the current dates are listed on their page.

orgs.name: Made by Momma

orgs.name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store
orgs.pickupNote: Their donations page states plainly: "Please note: We are unable to offer donation pick-up services." Worth knowing before you load a sofa — they do not take furniture at all.
orgs.locationsNote: A national chain. Their store locator at thriftstore.ca/locations is an interactive JavaScript tool, so individual Calgary stores could not be read from the site text and NO Calgary count or address is asserted here. Send readers to the locator to find their nearest Calgary drop-off.

metros.name: Edmonton
metros.localNote: Edmonton has exactly one confirmed free home-collection service for bulky household goods: Habitat for Humanity Edmonton's ReStore, which runs its own trucks across Edmonton, Beaumont, Fort Saskatchewan, Leduc (twice monthly), Nisku, St. Albert, Sherwood Park and Spruce Grove. Their own site states the crucial limit: "Due to safety regulations, we unfortunately cannot move any items from basements, nor can we enter homes." The sofa has to be at ground level or in the garage before they arrive. Beyond that, most Edmonton charities are drop-off only. Goodwill states plainly on its own site that it has no pickup service at all, despite operating 14 donation centres in the city. Find Edmonton will collect on weekends in surrounding areas but reserves the right to refuse items at the door, and its own page warns that items that don't qualify may be offered "disposal for a fee" - so cost is not guaranteed to be zero. Diabetes Canada's free pickup is a clothing-and-small-goods service only, on strict terms: sealed bags or boxes under 40 lbs on the doorstep, and "Loose items will not be collected."

orgs.name: Diabetes Canada - Declutter for Diabetes
refuses: Loose items - everything must be in sealed bags or boxes
Anything over 40 lbs per bag or box
Items left on the ground outside donation bins
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, but only when they have a scheduled run in your area — enter your postal code on their site to check. Items must be in sealed bags or boxes under 40 lb and left on the doorstep; loose items are not collected.
orgs.locationsNote: Donation bins plus drop-off through their Value Village partnership - Diabetes Canada's own site confirms the Value Village partnership, and the Value Village Community Donation Centre at 10127 34 Avenue NW, Edmonton lists Diabetes Canada as the nonprofit that receives the proceeds. Use the bin and drop-off finder at declutterfordiabetes.ca rather than assuming a location.

orgs.name: Edmonton Emergency Response and Newcomer Services (EERNS)
accepts: New or gently used household items
orgs.pickupNote: They arrange furniture pickups from your location. Email donations@eerns.ca to arrange. Their site does not state whether a fee applies or which areas are covered, so confirm both when you book.
orgs.locationsNote: Edmonton-based CRA-registered charity. Contact donations@eerns.ca to arrange a drop-off or pickup rather than turning up unannounced. A second line, (780) 700-2281, and Info@eerns.ca also appear on their site.

orgs.name: Edmonton's Food Bank
accepts: Non-perishable food - see the printable most-needed-items list on their site
refuses: No refusal list is published on their give-food page
orgs.pickupNote: Their site states: "To maximize our trucking resources, we can not arrange pick ups for small amounts of food (i.e. less than 100 lbs)." For donations over 100 lbs, contact them with at least 3 business days' notice so they can route a truck. Household-sized donations must be dropped off.
orgs.locationsNote: Main warehouse at 11508 120 Street NW, plus drop-off at local fire stations (ring the buzzer and leave donations with Edmonton Fire Service members), participating grocery stores, and community events. Note: 780-425-2133 is the general inquiries line. Their other published number, 780-425-4190, is the FOOD ASSISTANCE line for people seeking help - please do not use it for donations.

orgs.name: Electronic Recycling Association (ERA)
refuses: No outright refusal list is published. Note that TVs, microwaves and floor-model copiers/printers carry a fee rather than being free drop-offs.
orgs.pickupNote: Pickups are offered to both residents and businesses, Monday to Friday, and are aimed at larger quantities - their site says ERA "will dispatch a truck to pickup large quantities of electronics". Charges apply: "Any pickup charges applied to your donations are based on location, the number of items, service requirements." Drop-offs of standard computer equipment are often free. Budget for a fee unless the donation is high-value or high-volume. Working devices are refurbished and may be donated on to charities, schools and non-profits; secure data destruction is offered, priced from $0.00 to $5.00 per item depending on the equipment.
orgs.locationsNote: One Edmonton depot. Hours are not stated on their Edmonton page - call before driving. A toll-free line, 1-877-9EWASTE, also appears on their site. ERA operates in other Canadian cities too.
orgs.singleAddress: Unit 5, 14212 128 Ave NW, Edmonton, AB T5L 3H5

orgs.name: Find Edmonton
refuses: Large appliances - stoves, fridges, washers, dryers
Items that are damaged or need repair
orgs.pickupNote: Their own donation form page states: "We are happy to pick up of in the surrounding areas of Edmonton on weekends." Book at https://findedmonton.com/pages/donation-form or call 780-988-1717. Important caveat from the same page: "The Find trucking team have discretion not to accept an item if it does not meet our donation criteria" - and donors whose items do not qualify may be offered other options "for a fee". Whether the pickup itself is free is not stated, so confirm when you book.
orgs.locationsNote: One site: the Find Retail + Donation Centre. Hours listed as Monday-Saturday 9 a.m.-5 p.m., Sunday 12-5 p.m. (seasonal). Do not leave items outside business hours - their site says unattended items cannot be used. Find is partnered with Homeward Trust Edmonton and supports people moving out of homelessness. They also accept clothing on behalf of Bissell Centre, and act as an electronics recycling drop-off for Quantum Lifecycle Partners.

orgs.name: Habitat for Humanity Edmonton ReStore
orgs.pickupNote: Free donation pickup covering Edmonton, Beaumont, Fort Saskatchewan, Leduc (twice monthly), Nisku, St. Albert, Sherwood Park and Spruce Grove. Critical limitation stated on their own site: "Due to safety regulations, we unfortunately cannot move any items from basements, nor can we enter homes." Items must be accessible outside the home. Book through their online form or call (780) 477-4057.
orgs.locationsNote: 6 ReStores, confirmed on their own locations page: Edmonton North (8210 Yellowhead Trail NW), Edmonton West (16811 106 Avenue NW), Edmonton South (4004 99 Street NW), Leduc (Unit 222, 3601 82 Avenue), St. Albert (Unit 120, 730 St. Albert Trail) and Sherwood Park (7 Streambank Avenue). All open Monday-Sunday 9:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. and closed on all statutory holidays. Full list at https://hfh.org/restore/locations-hours/

orgs.name: Bissell Thrift Shop (Bissell Centre)
orgs.pickupNote: Pickup is not mentioned anywhere on their website that I could read - not on the home, donate, or locations pages, and the FAQ page is currently a dead link. Treat this as drop-off only unless you phone (780) 471-6644 and arrange otherwise. Do not assume a pickup exists.
orgs.locationsNote: Main store on Alberta Avenue: retail hours Monday-Sunday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., donation drop-off Monday-Sunday 10:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m., free parking. A second, CLOTHES-ONLY drop-off is hosted at FIND Edmonton, 5120 122 Street - check FIND's own hours before going there.

orgs.name: Edmonton Public Library
accepts: Gently used books - paperbacks and hardcovers
CDs, DVDs and audiobooks in their original packaging
Recent video games in their original packaging
Textbooks published within the last four years
Vinyl records in good condition with minimal scratches

CDs, DVDs, audiobooks or video games without their original packaging
Encyclopedias, magazines, specialized journals or outdated textbooks
Cassettes, VHS tapes, and burned CDs or DVDs

metros.name: Ottawa
metros.localNote: Ottawa's hard case is a sofa, and the reason is that the two biggest names take neither. The Salvation Army lists furniture on its cannot-accept list outright and states it is unable to offer any pickup at all; Diabetes Canada's Declutter will come to your door, but refuses all furniture and all beds. That leaves three realistic routes for large furniture, each with a different catch: Habitat ReStore (free pickup, but selective, one to two weeks' notice, and their form currently restricts pickup to kitchens and large appliances), Helping With Furniture (drop-off free, pickup carries a service fee and only inside their zone), and Matthew House Ottawa (drop-off by arrangement, pickup number published but no price or zones published anywhere). Across the river, Comptoir Saint-Vincent de Paul de Hull is the standout: it takes furniture, mattresses, fridges and stoves together, and its trucks collect in the Hull, Aylmer and Gatineau sectors. Its site is French-only. Two smaller routes are worth knowing because they save a trip: any Ottawa Public Library branch takes small book donations for FOPLA, and any Browns Cleaners location takes used children's snowsuits, launders them and delivers them to The Snowsuit Fund for you.

accepts: New and used clothing for babies, children and adults

Their trucks collect donated items in good condition in the Hull, Aylmer and Gatineau sectors — phone 819-776-1068 to arrange. No fee is stated for donation pickup; delivery of items you buy is offered at reasonable cost. Site is in French.

What distinguishes them from a shredder is that working devices are wiped and refurbished for donation rather than destroyed.

Kitchen and bathroom cabinets and fixtures
New building materials, residential hardware, plumbing and electrical supplies
Large and small functioning household appliances, and dishwashers with stainless steel interiors

New flooring, minimum 80 sq. ft., and new tiles, minimum 50 sq. ft.

Terms they do state: requests are answered in 24-48 hours, pickups generally need one to two weeks' notice, items must be ground level and accessible or have service elevator access, must be free of rips, stains, odours and pet hair, and the driver has final approval. Request form at https://habitatgo.com/restore/restore-pick-up-form/. They also advise calling before donating, since what they can take shifts with stock levels.

Food not prepared in a professional kitchen

Their stated limit is a 30-minute driving radius of the downtown location. Arrange it by emailing donate@sghottawa.com. Drop-offs are taken between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

orgs.name: The Ottawa Mission

Unopened deodorant, razors, toothbrushes and toothpaste
orgs.pickupNote: They can arrange donation pick-ups within Ottawa on request — call 613-234-1144 ext. 428 or email donations@ottawamission.com. Worth knowing before you load the car: this is a men's shelter with limited storage, and household goods, furniture and used clothing are all on the cannot-accept list. New items are what they are asking for.

orgs.name: Cornerstone Housing for Women

Questions go to donate@cornerstonewomen.ca or 613-254-6584 ext. 521.

Graphic novels, art books, classic literature

Signs of insect infestation or mould

orgs.name: Matthew House Ottawa — Furniture Bank
accepts: Beds in all sizes except king, dressers, mirrors, night tables
Couches, chairs, lamps, tables, dining chairs
refuses: Anything over 4' wide x 2' deep x 6' high
Worn or damaged furniture, including rips, tears and stains
orgs.pickupNote: Their donation page lists a separate pickup phone number, 1-613-423-2454, so a pickup route exists — but the site does not publish the price, the zones or the schedule anywhere I could reach, so call before you count on it. Drop-off is possible and must be arranged first: call 613-591-6681 ext. 2511 or email furnituredonations@matthewhouseottawa.org.
orgs.locationsNote: One furniture bank warehouse.

orgs.name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store / Donor Welcome Centre
orgs.pickupNote: They state it flatly: "We are unable to offer donation pick-up services." Everything has to be brought to a store or Donor Welcome Centre. The other thing people get wrong about the Salvation Army in Canada — furniture is on the cannot-accept list outright, so a sofa is not an option here at all.
orgs.locationsNote: The chain's own page cites over 120 locations across Canada without breaking out a count for Ottawa. Use their finder at https://thriftstore.ca/locations, which searches by city or postal code.

orgs.name: The Snowsuit Fund of Ottawa

The easier route for most people: leave used snowsuits at any Browns Cleaners location, where they are laundered, sanitized, bagged and delivered to the Fund for you. School and community groups can deliver to the Browns main plant on Bronson Ave, Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 8 am to 1 pm.

orgs.singleAddress: 225 Donald St, Unit 134, Ottawa, ON K1K 1N1

orgs.pickupNote: Drop-off only, at the Community Donation Centre attached to each store; no pickup service is mentioned. Value Village is a for-profit thrift retailer that pays a nonprofit partner for the goods you drop off, and the partner differs by location — the South Ottawa store at 1824 Bank St supports Diabetes Canada, per its own store page. Check the store page for the location nearest you before assuming which cause your donation funds.

metros.name: Winnipeg
metros.localNote: Winnipeg's biggest quirk is that Goodwill here is not the Goodwill people know from elsewhere - Canadian Goodwill Industries is a registered Manitoba non-profit, Canadian since 1931, with six Manitoba stores, all proceeds staying in the province, and genuinely free home pickup that takes furniture, mattresses and large freestanding appliances. Between it and Habitat ReStore, which offers free pickup within city limits, Winnipeggers have two no-cost options for heavy items, with Oyate Tipi as a paid-but-receipted third that will actually carry a sofa out of the house. The trap worth knowing: Salvation Army Thrift and Value Village take no furniture and do no pickups at all - Salvation Army says so in plain words on its own donation page. One genuinely local arrangement no national list would have: bikes and bike parts can be left at any City of Winnipeg 4R Depot, where the WRENCH collects them about twice a month.

Mattresses and box springs in clean condition
Mobility aids in clean working condition
Area rugs, lamps, pictures, seasonal items, patio furniture
refuses: Items that are dirty, ripped, stained, broken, missing pieces, pet- or smoke-damaged, rusty, or a health/safety hazard
Items from homes with evidence of pests, or treated for pests in the last 3 months
CRT computer monitors and console TVs
orgs.pickupNote: Free home pickup, booked by phone at (204) 943-6435, by email, or through their online request form, Monday to Friday 8am-4pm. Pickup runs on a city district schedule that sets which day your area is served, and you get a confirmation email with your date within 48 business hours. Service covers Winnipeg and select nearby Manitoba communities. All donations are inspected for rodent and insect activity - they will not collect from a home that has had pest activity or extermination in the last 3 months. Read their pickup terms and conditions before booking.
orgs.locationsNote: A registered Manitoba non-profit charity, Canadian since 1931, with six thrift stores across Manitoba and all proceeds staying in Manitoba. Head office 70 Princess Street, Winnipeg. Use their Locations & Hours page for store addresses.

orgs.name: Diabetes Canada - Declutter for Diabetes
accepts: Cameras, cell phones, PDAs, laptops, tablets
Small household appliances (blenders, irons, hand mixers)
Cookware, bakeware, cutlery and utensils, tableware, barware
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, but only when they have a scheduled run in your area — enter your postal code on their site to check. Items must be in sealed bags or boxes under 40 lb and left on the doorstep; loose items are not collected.
orgs.locationsNote: A national home pick-up service. Diabetes Canada is also the named non-profit partner at four Winnipeg Value Village donation centres (Nairn, Jefferson, Pembina and Ellice), so dropping off there supports them. Book a pickup at https://declutterfordiabetes.ca/pickup

orgs.name: Electronic Recycling Association (ERA)
orgs.pickupNote: They do send trucks across Winnipeg to collect electronics from offices, warehouses, schools and residential addresses, booked online or by phone - but pickup is not automatically free. Cost depends on your location, the number of items and the level of service required, and fees are frequently waived during promotions and for members or high-value donations. For a single old laptop, drop it off instead.
orgs.locationsNote: One Winnipeg depot. Most drop-offs in Winnipeg are free, but fees apply to microwaves, televisions and floor-model copiers and printers. Secure data destruction runs $0-$5 per item. Toll-free 1-877-9EWASTE.

orgs.name: Habitat for Humanity Manitoba ReStore
accepts: Renovation materials and hardware (clean, no nails, 8 feet and over)
Windows up to 6 ft (no sealed units)
Kitchen and modular cabinets, medicine cabinets
Appliances - washers, dryers and stoves, 7 years old or less
Bathroom fixtures, claw foot tubs (no rust)
refuses: Wooden dining room tables with matching chairs
Lumber with nails in it or under 8 feet
orgs.pickupNote: Free pickup of donations and larger items within city limits, including curbside. Items must be readily accessible - outside or in a garage; crews do not retrieve items from basements or other levels. A ReStore driver inspects each item and makes the final decision on what is taken. Book by calling Sheila at (204) 233-5160 ext. 220.
orgs.locationsNote: Three ReStores in Manitoba - two in Winnipeg (60 Archibald St., 204-233-5160, and 1565 Inkster Blvd., 204-414-0603) plus Brandon. Locations and hours: https://www.habitat.mb.ca/restore/location-hours/

orgs.name: Oyate Tipi Cumini Yape
accepts: Flat-screen TVs; tube TVs up to 26 inches
orgs.pickupNote: They will come and carry it out, but pickup is a paid service - they describe their rates as competitive, 100% of the fee goes to their charity operations, you pay no HST, and you receive a charitable tax receipt for the value of the furniture. Request a pickup through their site or call. For a sofa you cannot move yourself, this is usually the realistic Winnipeg option.
orgs.locationsNote: A Winnipeg furniture bank that redistributes household goods to people setting up a home. Main location 606 Selkirk Ave, phone hours Mon-Fri 8-5 and Sat-Sun 8-3. Separate donation drop-off at 429 Dufferin Ave, Mon-Fri 9am-4pm.

orgs.name: Centre Flavie
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is described on their donations page - it asks donors to bring items to 301 Archibald Street. Call 204-231-9513 before assuming a truck will come.
orgs.locationsNote: One location. Goods are given free to people in need. The published hours, Monday to Friday 9am-1pm, are the client hours; donor drop-off hours are not separately stated, so phone ahead.

orgs.name: Harvest Manitoba
orgs.pickupNote: No home pickup is advertised. Drop off at 1085 Winnipeg Avenue, Monday to Friday 8:30am-4:30pm and Saturday 9am-3pm, closed Sunday. Worth knowing when you are clearing a pantry during a move.
orgs.locationsNote: Central Winnipeg warehouse. Their donate-food page does not state how many agencies they supply, so do not quote a number.

orgs.name: MCC Thrift (Mennonite Central Committee)
accepts: Media - records, tapes, CDs, DVDs and videos
refuses: Damaged items - dirty, broken, stained, smoky, smelling, or with excessive pet hair
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is stated on their donation page. Three categories are decided shop by shop rather than centrally - e-waste (computers, TVs, phones), seasonal items, and mattresses - so call your nearest shop before loading the car. Furniture is taken at limited locations only.
orgs.locationsNote: Four MCC Thrift shops in Winnipeg: Kildonan MCC Thrift Shop, Sargent MCC Thrift Shop, MCC Furniture Thrift Shop, and Selkirk Ave MCC Furniture & Thrift Shop, plus a dozen more across Manitoba. Addresses and phone numbers are not on the shop list itself - use the shop finder at https://mccthrift.com/locations

orgs.name: Siloam Mission
accepts: Move-Out Kits - household starter kits for people moving into housing
Items shipped directly from their Amazon wish list
Other urgently needed goods - their current needs list changes, so check the page or ask before loading up
refuses: Food items, over-the-counter medications, or hygiene items that have been opened or have expired
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is offered. Drop off at Shipping & Receiving, 300 Princess St, entrance on Henry Ave, Monday to Saturday 8am-4pm, closed Sundays, holidays and long weekends. Email donategoods@siloam.ca or call 204-956-4344 before bringing a large load or to ask what is needed right now.
orgs.locationsNote: One donation receiving location in downtown Winnipeg. Tax receipts are issued in Canadian dollars and exclude PST, GST and shipping per CRA guidelines.
orgs.singleAddress: 300 Princess Street (entrance on Henry Avenue), Winnipeg, MB

orgs.name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store
refuses: Infant equipment such as car seats, cribs and strollers
orgs.pickupNote: Their own donation page states plainly: they are unable to offer donation pick-up services. Everything must be dropped off at a store or Donor Welcome Centre. This is the most common mistake people make with Salvation Army in Canada - and note they take no furniture, beds or large appliances at all.
orgs.locationsNote: Over 120 locations across Canada. Their site does not publish a province list - enter your city or postal code in the store locator at https://thriftstore.ca/locations to find a store or Donor Welcome Centre near you.

orgs.name: The WRENCH (Winnipeg Repair Education and Cycling Hub)
orgs.pickupNote: Their FAQ states they are unable to offer pick-ups of donations at this time. Drop off at their Logan Ave shop, or leave bikes and parts at any City of Winnipeg 4R Depot - the WRENCH checks the depots roughly twice a month. They do not control depot hours, so check those before you go.
orgs.locationsNote: Main shop at 1057 Logan Ave, Winnipeg, plus collection through Winnipeg's 4R Depots. Email info@thewrench.ca

orgs.name: Union Gospel Mission Winnipeg - Box of Blessings
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is advertised. They run a network of Box of Blessings donation bins - some still labelled TOSS BOXES - hosted at churches, businesses and community centres, and the full bin list with addresses is on their donation page.
orgs.locationsNote: Around 50 Box of Blessings bin locations listed across Winnipeg and rural Manitoba, including Oakbank, Selkirk, Stonewall, Steinbach, Carman, Portage la Prairie and Winkler. UGM's own Charis Centre is at 271 Archibald Street, Winnipeg. Registered charity 119275758RR0001. Programme contact: Martin Chidwick, 204-943-9904 ext. 237.

orgs.name: Value Village (Savers) Community Donation Centre
orgs.pickupNote: Drop-off only at the Community Donation Centre attached to each store; no pickup is offered. This is a for-profit retailer that pays a non-profit partner for what you drop off, and the partner differs by store - so if you care which charity benefits, check which one your nearest store is paired with first.
orgs.locationsNote: Six Winnipeg stores, each listing its own non-profit partner: 3629 Portage Ave (Big Brothers Big Sisters of Winnipeg), 970 Nairn Ave, 942 Jefferson Ave, 1729 Pembina Hwy and 1695 Ellice Ave (all Diabetes Canada), and 1731 Kenaston Blvd Suite B (Canadian Red Cross). Store finder: https://stores.savers.com/mb/winnipeg/
orgs.notCharity: A for-profit retailer, not a charity. It pays a nonprofit partner for donated goods — the partner differs by store, so ask at the door if that matters to you.

metros.name: Québec City
metros.localNote: À Québec, la cueillette gratuite de meubles à domicile repose sur deux organismes que nous avons pu confirmer sur leur propre site: le Comptoir Emmaüs (418-692-0385, à partir de 5 boîtes/sacs ou pour tout meuble) et le Centre Ozanam de la Société de Saint-Vincent-de-Paul (418 522-0880, gratuit, ville de Québec seulement, du mardi au samedi). Le SEBV (418 683-4083) ramasse aussi des meubles, mais uniquement sur sélection: on décrit l'article, l'atelier décide s'il vient le chercher. Attention aux fausses pistes courantes: Entraide diabétique du Québec fait bien de la collecte à domicile dans la Capitale-Nationale, mais refuse explicitement « les meubles en tout genre », et Renaissance écrit noir sur blanc qu'elle n'offre pas de cueillette à domicile en magasin. Pour les livres, la Bibliothèque de Québec accepte les dons au comptoir de n'importe quelle succursale; pour les ordinateurs, OPEQ a un atelier dans le parc industriel Armand-Viau.

orgs.name: Entraide diabétique du Québec (EDQ)
accepts: Sacs à main et sacs à dos, valises
Équipements électroniques fonctionnels, caméras, radios, horloges
Fer à repasser, fer à friser, séchoir à cheveux
Jeux de société, jouets, articles de sport
refuses: Armes à feu ou armes blanches
Vêtements tachés, troués ou en mauvais état

On s'inscrit par formulaire en ligne et l'organisme rappelle pour convenir d'une date. La liste exacte des municipalités desservies est sur https://entraidediabetique.org/collecte/. Leur site n'indique pas si le service est payant. Important: ils refusent explicitement les « meubles en tout genre » — ne comptez pas sur eux pour un sofa. Québec: 418 877-5111 ou 1 888 877-5111.
orgs.locationsNote: Boîtes de dons et centres de dons en magasin répartis au Québec — consulter leur carte des centres de dons sur leur site plutôt que de se fier à un nombre. Les dons déposés au centre de dons Village des Valeurs de Sainte-Foy vont à EDQ (confirmé sur le site de Village des Valeurs).

orgs.name: Moisson Québec
accepts: Produits comestibles secs (pâtes, conserves, condiments, breuvages)
Produits non comestibles (produits d'hygiène, produits pour bébés)
refuses: Aliments et breuvages pour bébés périmés
Tout aliment détérioré, de couleur ou d'odeur douteuse
orgs.pickupNote: « Nous offrons le transport des dons sous certaines conditions, contactez-nous pour plus de détails. » 418-682-5061 ou operations@moissonquebec.com. Source lue: https://moissonquebec.com/don-de-denrees/
orgs.locationsNote: Un seul entrepôt. Dépôt du lundi au vendredi, 8 h à 11 h 30 et 13 h à 15 h 30, sur rendez-vous. Banque alimentaire: denrées et produits d'hygiène seulement, pas de biens usagés.

orgs.name: OPEQ – Ordinateurs pour les écoles du Québec
orgs.pickupNote: Cueillette gratuite à partir de 15 appareils; pour de plus petites quantités, il faut les contacter pour convenir d'une solution. Ils acceptent les dons de particuliers autant que d'entreprises. Dons: 1 877 617-6737 (option 1) ou don@opeq.qc.ca. Source lue: https://www.opeq.qc.ca/donner/
orgs.locationsNote: Cinq ateliers au Québec (Montréal, Québec, Saguenay, Sherbrooke, Gatineau). Celui de la Capitale-Nationale: 6665, rue Zéphirin-Paquet, porte D (livraisons par les portes K1, K2 ou K3), parc industriel Armand-Viau, Québec, QC G2C 0M2 — 418 843-5963, atq@opeq.qc.ca, lun–ven 7 h à 15 h 30. Source: https://www.opeq.qc.ca/en/contact-us/

orgs.name: SEBV – Service d'entraide Basse-Ville
accepts: Meubles (sélectionnés selon les besoins de l'atelier)
Articles divers (chute de dons extérieure accessible 24/7)
orgs.pickupNote: Cueillette de meubles et d'électroménagers seulement, et uniquement sur sélection: on décrit les articles au coordonnateur de l'atelier des meubles (photo appréciée) et celui-ci détermine ce qu'il ira chercher. Territoire desservi: ville de Québec. Atelier des meubles: 418 683-4083. Leur site précise que l'atelier « ne remplace en aucun cas la cueillette des encombrants de la Ville de Québec ». Source lue: https://sebv.ca/donner/
orgs.singleAddress: 155, av. du Sacré-Coeur, Québec, QC G1N 2W3
orgs.locationsNote: Adresse principale confirmée: 155, av. du Sacré-Coeur. Vêtements et objets: chute de dons extérieure accessible en tout temps; articles volumineux ou fragiles à apporter durant les heures d'ouverture. Autres numéros publiés sur leur page de dons: 418-529-6889 (dépannage alimentaire) et 367-380-6496 (magasin de meubles).

orgs.name: Bibliothèque de Québec
accepts: Documents en très bonne condition publiés dans les 15 dernières années
refuses: Livres vendus par les clubs de livres
orgs.pickupNote: Dépôt seulement, au comptoir de n'importe laquelle de leurs bibliothèques. Pour un don important (plus de 100 documents ou 3 boîtes), il faut contacter la Bibliothèque de Québec au préalable pour l'informer de la nature du don et de la date de livraison. Source lue: https://www.bibliothequedequebec.qc.ca/politiques/dons.aspx
orgs.locationsNote: Réseau de bibliothèques municipales: les dons se déposent au comptoir de n'importe quelle succursale. Voir leur site pour la liste des succursales.

orgs.name: Café Rencontre Centre-Ville
accepts: Bijoux et vêtements de très bonne qualité, apportés directement à la friperie
orgs.pickupNote: Dépôt seulement: dans leurs boîtes de dons réparties dans la ville de Québec, ou directement à la friperie (bijoux et articles de très bonne qualité, du lundi au vendredi entre 10 h et 16 h). Aucun service de cueillette n'est annoncé. Source lue: https://www.caferencontre.org/portfolio/friperie/
orgs.singleAddress: 810, rue Saint-Joseph Est, Québec, QC G1K 3C9

accepts: Meubles de salon, de chambre et de cuisine en bon état
Disques vinyle et systèmes de son
orgs.pickupNote: Collection is referred to on their site but the terms were not something we could confirm. Ask when you call.
orgs.singleAddress: 860, rue du Roi, Québec, QC G1K 2Y2
orgs.locationsNote: Un seul centre, dans Saint-Roch. Magasin ouvert du mardi au samedi, 10 h à 17 h. Un bac de cueillette extérieur est aussi offert.

orgs.name: Comptoir Emmaüs
accepts: Tout type d'objet en bon état
refuses: Tout objet trop lourd à transporter par deux personnes ou posant un risque de sécurité
orgs.pickupNote: Collection is referred to on their site but the terms were not something we could confirm. Ask when you call.
orgs.singleAddress: 915, rue Saint-Vallier Est, Québec, QC G1K 3P9
orgs.locationsNote: Un seul comptoir. Heures confirmées sur leur site: lun–mer 9 h–17 h, jeu–ven 10 h–18 h, sam 10 h–17 h, fermé le dimanche. Les dons de meubles entrent par une porte distincte (4e étage, Côte de la Potasse, porte 4).

orgs.name: La Bouchée Généreuse

Horaire affiché sur cette page: lun–mar 9 h–12 h et 13 h–16 h, mer 9 h–12 h et 13 h–19 h, jeudi fermé, ven 9 h–12 h et 12 h 30–15 h. Leur site affiche ailleurs un horaire légèrement différent: appeler avant de se déplacer.

orgs.name: Renaissance

orgs.pickupNote: Leur page de dons est explicite: « Please note that we do not offer home pick-ups. » Un service distinct d'inscription à une collecte à domicile existe à collecteadomicile.renaissancequebec.ca avec vérification par code postal, mais cette page ne s'est pas chargée lors de la vérification — l'admissibilité des codes postaux de Québec n'est PAS confirmée. Apportez vos articles en magasin. Ils précisent aussi que la liste d'articles n'est pas exhaustive et que le préposé peut refuser un article.
orgs.locationsNote: Renaissance est présente dans la région de Québec: quatre points confirmés sur leur propre carte (Charlesbourg, Halles Fleur de Lys, Laurier Québec et un centre de dons route de l'Église) plus un à Lévis. Utiliser leur localisateur officiel pour les adresses et heures à jour: https://renaissancequebec.ca/en/map/

orgs.name: Société Saint-Vincent-de-Paul de Québec (SSVPQ)

Consulter cette page pour les adresses et les heures — nous ne les reproduisons pas ici.

orgs.name: Village des Valeurs

orgs.pickupNote: La page du centre de dons n'annonce que des heures de dépôt sur place; aucun service de cueillette n'y est mentionné dans un sens ni dans l'autre.

D'autres succursales existent dans la région — utiliser leur localisateur de magasins. Les dons déposés ici soutiennent Entraide diabétique du Québec.

metros.name: Hamilton
metros.localNote: Two things are genuinely Hamilton-specific and both are verified on the operators' own sites. First, Drop 'n' Shop is run by Community Living Hamilton in partnership with the City, sited at the East Mountain Community Recycling Centre at 37 Kilbride Rd — so the good things and the rest go in one trip, and donation hours there run 8am–6pm, an hour either side of the store's own 9am–5pm. Second, if you have furniture, the picture narrows fast: the only at-the-door collection this check could confirm for Hamilton is St. Vincent de Paul's Parkdale store, whose own page states free pickup across upper and lower Hamilton, Ancaster, Dundas, Stoney Creek, Waterdown, Aldershot, Burlington and Oakville. Habitat ReStore takes large building materials and furniture but does not describe a pickup service — it only publishes a pickup contact, so call before assuming. Everyone else verified here is drop-off only or silent on the question. Do not write that "most national chains refuse furniture" as a Hamilton fact: the chains whose refusal lists say that (Salvation Army, Talize, Diabetes Canada) are not all confirmed to operate here.

orgs.name: St. Vincent de Paul Society — Hamilton Parkdale Store
refuses: No list of refused items is published on their site. Call the store before bringing large or unusual items.
orgs.pickupNote: Free pickup is stated on their own store page, with the service area given as "Hamilton (upper/lower), Ancaster, Dundas, Stoney Creek, Waterdown, Aldershot, Burlington and Oakville." Book by phone.
orgs.locationsNote: Their site lists three stores: Hamilton – Parkdale, Hamilton West – Barton St, and Dunnville. Only the Parkdale page loaded, so only its details are published here; link readers to https://ssvphamiltonpc.org/ for the others. Parkdale hours as published: Tue–Fri 10:00am–4:30pm, Sat 10:00am–4:00pm (donations accepted Sat 10:00am–2:00pm), closed Sunday and Monday.
orgs.singleAddress: 200 Parkdale Avenue North at Britannia, Hamilton, ON

orgs.name: ACCESS Tech (McMaster University / Empowerment Squared)
orgs.pickupNote: DOWNGRADED from the researcher's "conditional". Their page says to email AccTech@mcmaster.ca "to arrange a pick-up or drop-off of items on campus" — that is campus collection, not a home pickup, and nothing on the page says they will come to a residential address. Email first.
orgs.locationsNote: Run on McMaster's campus. The page states "McMaster-owned and personal technology is welcome," which is why this is included as open to the public — but it does not spell out a public drop-off point, so tell readers to email before travelling.
orgs.restricted: University drop-off logistics rather than a residential donation service.

orgs.name: Drop 'n' Shop Thrift Store (Community Living Hamilton)
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is mentioned on their site. Drop-off only.
orgs.locationsNote: A single non-profit store, "operated by Community Living Hamilton, in partnership with the City of Hamilton," sited at the East Mountain Community Recycling Centre. Donation hours (Mon–Sat 8:00am–6:00pm) are longer than store hours (Mon–Sat 9:00am–5:00pm); closed Sunday.

orgs.name: Good Shepherd Centres
accepts: Lightly used and clean seasonal clothing and footwear
Small appliances and electronics (less than 5 years old)

orgs.locationsNote: Drop-off is at 155 Cannon Street East, Hamilton, 9:00am–3:00pm Monday to Friday. This address is the publicly advertised donation drop-off published on their own donate page, not a shelter location — Good Shepherd's residential and women's services addresses are not listed here and must not be added.

orgs.name: Goodwill, Ontario Great Lakes
refuses: Large furniture and heavy items over 50 lbs
Items that have been recalled or banned, or do not meet current safety standards
orgs.pickupNote: No pickup service is described anywhere on their donation page — it describes taking donations to a Donation Centre, where "our Donation Attendant will be there to accept your donation."
orgs.locationsNote: Hamilton presence confirmed on their own About page, which names Hamilton among the regions they operate in. Their locator page states they operate "over 45 Donation Centres across Southern Ontario" but the interactive list does not render, so no Hamilton address could be read. Link to https://www.goodwillindustries.ca/donation-centre-locator/ and let readers search.

orgs.name: Habitat for Humanity Hamilton ReStore
accepts: New flooring / ceramic tile (minimum 80 sq. ft.)
refuses: No list of refused items is published on their site. Contact the ReStore before bringing anything large or unusual.
orgs.pickupNote: DOWNGRADED from the researcher's "conditional". Neither their donation page nor their ReStore page describes a pickup service, free or paid. What is on the page is a pickup contact: restorepickups@habitathamilton.ca and 905-560-6707 ext. 104. Email or call to ask whether they will collect and on what terms — do not promise readers a pickup.
orgs.locationsNote: Two ReStores, both addresses confirmed on their own site: 285 Nash Road North, Unit 1, Hamilton, ON L8H 7P4 and 1525 Stone Church Rd E, Hamilton, ON L8W 3P8. DO NOT PUBLISH HOURS: their own two pages contradict each other — the donation page says Mon–Sat 9am–5pm, the ReStore page says Mon–Fri 10am–6pm, Sat 9am–5pm. Tell readers to check the site or phone ahead.

orgs.name: Safetynet Charities

Confirm terms at furniture@safetynetservices.ca or 905-845-7233.

orgs.name: Talize

Very dirty, wet or broken items

orgs.locationsNote: Their own locations page lists 15 stores (13 in Ontario, 2 in BC) and Hamilton is one of them, but the Hamilton address and donation hours did not render. Link to https://talize.com/locations/ rather than publishing an address.

orgs.name: Value Village (Hamilton — Fennell Avenue)

orgs.singleAddress: 530 Fennell Avenue East, Hamilton, ON L8V 1S9
orgs.notCharity: A for-profit retailer, not a charity. It pays a nonprofit partner for donated goods — the partner differs by store, so ask at the door if that matters to you.

metros.name: Kitchener–Waterloo
metros.localNote: The most useful local fact is MCC Picks Up (mccpicksup.com, 226-220-0088), a home pickup service run by Mennonite Central Committee that books online and covers, in their words, "the Region of Waterloo and some outlier communities." Two hard limits: it will NOT take furniture, and nothing may exceed 50 lb per container. Their FAQ does not state a price, so ask when you book. For furniture that genuinely needs collecting, the free option is St Vincent de Paul in Cambridge (one week's notice, main-floor access only, pickups Monday to Friday 9 a.m.-2 p.m.); Habitat for Humanity Guelph Wellington advertises free pickup outright; Habitat Waterloo Region takes pickup requests but warns that not all will qualify; and Mission Thrift Store Kitchener charges a flat $30 and collects from your curb. One trap catches people here: the Salvation Army thrift chain in Canada accepts neither furniture nor mattresses and states plainly that it offers no pickup at all, despite being most people's first guess. Mattresses are refused nearly everywhere - Worth A Second Look, run by The Working Centre at 37 Market Lane in downtown Kitchener, is the notable exception that lists mattresses and beds among what it accepts.

metros.name: London
metros.localNote: London's practical problem is furniture. Only two organizations on this page will come to a house for it, and only one of them — St. Vincent de Paul — will take an actual couch, on a fixed neighbourhood rota (Monday northeast, Tuesday northwest, Thursday southwest, Friday southeast). Habitat's no-cost collection is a pre-renovation salvage crew for cabinets, doors and sinks, not a moving service. Everyone else in this city refuses furniture outright: Diabetes Canada, Talize and Goodwill all name it explicitly, and Goodwill draws the line at 50 lbs. So the honest shape of a London page is: furniture goes to SSVP or it goes in a truck to TRY Recycling and costs money; clothing and small goods have four good homes; electronics that nobody wants go to the EPRA finder.

That is a pre-renovation fixture salvage, not a couch pickup. Ordinary donations go through the London donation form at https://www.habitat4home.ca/london-donation-form, where you upload photos first; the form does not state whether a pickup or a drop-off follows. Phone the store before loading a vehicle.

This is still the right destination for the TVs, monitors and dead electronics that Diabetes Canada, Goodwill and the thrift chains all turn away.

metros.name: Victoria
metros.localNote: Only two organizations in Greater Victoria will collect large furniture from your home, and both charge rather than doing it free: Habitat for Humanity Victoria ReStore at $50, and WIN at $40 plus GST. In both cases the fee is non-refundable and does not guarantee your sofa is accepted - crews assess items at the door - so email photos ahead and book about a week out. Everything else on this page is effectively drop-off. Big Brothers Big Sisters states outright that it cannot pick up donations. St Vincent de Paul describes no pickup at all. Beacon asks you to fill in a furniture form or phone a shop, but does not publish what that service involves or costs, so call before you count on it. Two conditions come up again and again and are worth reading before you load the car: upholstered furniture generally has to come from a smoke-free and pet-free home (both ReStore and WIN say so), and almost every shop reserves final say at the drop-off door based on condition and how full the store already is.

orgs.name: Habitat for Humanity Victoria ReStore
accepts: New and gently used furniture (couches, chairs, tables, bed frames)
refuses: Large pieces of granite, stone or marble
Patio doors, flat panel doors, bi-fold or mirrored closet doors
orgs.pickupNote: Pickup is offered within Greater Victoria for complete kitchens, large furniture, major appliances, or corporate donations. A $50 non-refundable truck usage fee applies, stated as effective January 1, 2026. Book at least one week in advance. The fee does not guarantee acceptance: "Our experienced teams will assess donations at the time of pick-up" and "The ReStore team has final discretion on what items we can accept." Items must be free of rips, tears and stains and come from a smoke-free and pet-free home.
orgs.locationsNote: Two ReStores: 721 Vanalman Ave, Victoria BC and 849 Orono Ave, Langford BC. Donation drop-off Monday to Saturday 9:30am-5:00pm, Sunday 11:00am-5:00pm. All donations are assessed at drop-off and the Receiving Team determines acceptance based on item condition and current store stock.

Pieces they cannot take due to limited warehouse and store space
orgs.pickupNote: Truck pickup covers the "Central Victoria Area" only and carries a non-refundable $40 + GST truck usage fee. Email photos of your items to win@womeninneed.ca first so they can tell you whether the pieces are likely to be accepted. The fee does not guarantee acceptance.

Furniture goes through the Home Shop at 1803 Cook St. Administrative office is 785 Pandora Ave, Victoria BC V8W 1N9 (250-480-4006) - not a drop-off point. Their charitable status and tax receipting are not stated on the pages checked; ask them directly if you need a receipt.

Computer monitors, keyboards and mice (up to 10 years old)

metros.name: Saskatoon
metros.localNote: Saskatoon runs a genuinely useful municipal reuse programme, Curbside Swap. You place gently used unwanted items at the curb in front of your property with a "free" sign, and the rest of the city goes treasure hunting. The next city-wide swap is Saturday, September 12, 2026, and city-promoted events happen annually on the first Saturday in June and the second Saturday in September - but you can host a neighbourhood swap any time of year, and the City provides printable "free stuff" signs, rules and guidelines, and a listings page so people can find your street. Details at saskatoon.ca/services-residents/waste-recycling/community-programs/curbside-swap, or 306-975-2487. For a furniture-sized load where you need someone to come to you, the Habitat ReStore on Avenue D South is the one confirmed free curbside pickup on this list - everything else here is drop-off, or doorstep-only with a 40 lb bag limit and no furniture.

accepts: Clothing, shoes, boots, accessories and bags

Cookware, bakeware, cutlery, barware and tableware
Small appliances such as blenders, irons and hand mixers
Cameras, cell phones, laptops and tablets
orgs.pickupNote: Free home collection, but only when they have a scheduled run in your area — enter your postal code on their site to check. Items must be in sealed bags or boxes under 40 lb and left on the doorstep; loose items are not collected.
orgs.locationsNote: Saskatoon presence confirmed by searching their own bin finder at https://declutterfordiabetes.ca/donation-bin, which returned five Saskatoon donation bins within about 2 km of the city centre, including sites on Duchess St, Campus Dr, Osler St and Cumberland Ave S. Bin locations change, so link the finder rather than any one bin. Separately, the Value Village donation door at 302 Cope Lane benefits Diabetes Canada, per the Savers locator.

Most major appliances in working order (Saskatoon store specifically)

Personal and portable audio and video systems

orgs.notCharity: A regulated recycling programme, not a charity. Electronics are dismantled and recycled, not reused.
